purpose: Answer the Nov 24 checker review, point 3: worst case of each running E0089 loop against the budgets.yaml limit of 100 CPU-hours per run.
method: Each job runs on 1 CPU, so its CPU time is at most its wall time (job 164655: 57.49 CPU-h in 57.49 h wall; step 84: 172,810 CPU-s in 173,491 s wall). Upper bounds therefore use wall time from the job's run-folder timestamp. The current step's start is the time its summary.json stub was written (mirror mtime). Completed Hatteras steps are those whose summary was written after the job started. In-step progress is not visible: logs and counters of the running step are written only at its end.
conclusion: If every running loop stops on the cap at its current step, as f* 0.33 and 0.57 did, the largest job total is f* 0.44 at about 97.6 CPU-hours (in 4.6 since Nov 24 07:05Z; it had used about 49.6 hours before that). The others stop at about 58 to 82 hours. A loop that finishes its current step inside the cap moves on with another 48 hours allowed, and can pass 100. No job can pass 100 CPU-hours before Nov 26 09:27Z (100 hours of wall time after it started).
guard: D0072: a timer wakes this line at about Nov 26 07:30Z. At that run, any E0089 job still running that is in a step above the one listed here is cancelled with program cancel before 09:27Z. A job still in its listed step and due to hit the cap before 100 hours (only f* 0.44, cap about Nov 26 07:05 to 07:30Z, job total about 97.6) is left to stop on its own; if it is still running at 09:00Z, it is cancelled.
